title: How to Explain Your AI Project in an Interview
content:
Your AI project is probably good enough to get you hired.
The way you explain it is what's holding you back.
Here is a simple five-part structure.
Most people say something like, "I built a chatbot using an API."
The interviewer nods, and forgets it in ten seconds.
Because that sentence tells them what you used, not what you can do.
Tools change every month. The way you think about a problem is what they are hiring.
So let's fix the story, one part at a time.
Part ONE. The problem.
Start with a person and a pain.
Say, "A support team spent hours searching policy documents for every ticket."
Now they care, before you mention a single tool.
Part TWO. The architecture.
Draw it in five boxes or less.
Documents go in, they are split and indexed, the right parts are retrieved, and the model answers with sources.
If you can't draw it simply, you don't understand it yet.
Now here's the part that actually separates you from other candidates.
Part THREE. The trade-offs.
Why this model and not a bigger one? Why this database?
Maybe a smaller model was cheaper and fast enough for the task.
Trade-offs show judgment, and judgment is what companies pay for.
Part FOUR. The failures.
Tell them exactly where it still breaks.
"It struggles with scanned tables, so I added a check that flags them for a human."
Honest limits make you look senior, not weak.
Part FIVE. What's next.
One or two clear improvements, and how you would measure them.
This shows you think like an engineer who ships, not a student who submits.
So write this down. Problem, architecture, trade-offs, failures, next.
Practice it in two minutes, and then in thirty seconds.
Put the same structure in your README and on LinkedIn.
Because a project nobody understands is a project nobody hires for.
